subject: Manual implementation of sparse BYM2 model - how to set latent effect of size 2*n

messages.author: de99922251954296
messages.subject: Manual implementation of sparse BYM2 model - how to set latent effect of size 2*n
parts:
Dear INLA experts

In order to fit a multivariate BYM2 model I am trying to implement the sparse parametrization manually. It is possible in theory by using a similar argument to Riebler et al. (2016), i.e. modelling jointly the BYM field and the ICAR component.

The problem is that the latent effect length is twice observations length, though only the first half enters the linear predictor.

So, before working the multivariate model out, I am trying to implement manually (i.e. with inla.rgeneric.define() ) the univariate BYM to try replicating roughly what the precompiled f(..., model = "bym2" ) function call does. It is a divide-and-conquer approach.

However, I cannot find a way to fit a model where the latent effect is twice the size of observations. I tried inla.stack() as with the SPDE model, where the latent field has indeed a higher dimension, but in this case INLA crashes and I cannot figure out the exact problem from the log.
Could somebody please help me setting a latent effect of size 2n?

Thank you very much. I attach an application example
Best,
LC

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Manual implementation of sparse BYM2 model - how to set latent effect of size 2*n
parts:
it shouldn't be a problem. 'idx' at

f(idx, model=your.rgeneric)

can still be 1:n while your model 'your.rgeneric' can be of size 2*n
